storylines.title: France riots and European unrest
storylines.summary: French protests are in their fifth week. Unions staged a nationwide strike Thursday; the interior ministry counted 600,000 marchers, unions said more, and 70,000 police were deployed. Budget talks remain deadlocked. Earlier clashes hit Paris and Marseille; violent protests also hit German cities.

events.text: Unions stage a general strike; the interior ministry estimates 600,000 marchers nationwide, with unions citing a far higher number.
France braces for a nationwide strike and marches over cost of living and education as parliamentary budget talks remain deadlocked.
France opens an attempted-murder investigation after petrol bombs are thrown at riot police at Saturday's protests; no arrests reported.
Germany's cost-of-living protests turn violent in Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt, with shops looted, the same day hundreds of thousands protest in France.
Police clash with masked rioters in Paris, Marseille and other cities after largely peaceful third-wave marches across France.
Macron bans 'illegitimate' protests; total ban in Marseille and Lyon, union-organised marches only elsewhere, museums closed Saturday.
France's 10-year borrowing costs reach 5% for the first time since 2002, the FT reports.
Macron accuses Trump and other foreign leaders of 'stupid comments' about the unrest as France readies for more protests this weekend.
France announces nightly curfews in Paris, Lyon and other cities for as long as necessary after the first quiet night.
EU regulators probe pro-Kremlin disinformation and the role of social platforms around the French riots, the FT reports.
Italy approves sending 500 troops to Milan after clashes and protests.

storylines.title: US-Ukraine rift over Starlink and strikes
storylines.summary: Ukraine says at least 40 died in a Russian strike on Komyshuvakha. Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian delegations Thursday and urged a lasting truce; US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi are set for Nov. 10-11.

events.text: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House and urges them to build on the recent local truce.
Zelenskyy says he spoke for 90 minutes with Witkoff and Kushner ahead of trilateral talks; he and EU officials hope a Democratic Congress will help.
Kyiv says bodycam video shows a double-tap Russian strike on Komyshuvakha; at least 40 are dead and about 30 may be under rubble.
Zelenskyy says 40 are confirmed dead after a Russian strike on a school in Komyshuvakha; Kyiv releases bodycam video.
Russian and Ukrainian delegations are to meet Melania Trump at the White House Thursday after the Oleshky ceasefire.
Russian attacks on an aid centre, hospice and hospital kill at least 38 in 24 hours; Zelenskyy says dozens may be trapped.
US Air Force asks industry to mass produce the Extended Range Attack Munition cruise missile for Ukraine.
Witkoff announces US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, restarting a track suspended in February.
Russian bombs hit an aid centre and shelter in southern Ukraine, killing at least 26; Zelenskyy calls the attack vile.
Air raid alert apps in Ukraine and Russia are hit by cyberattacks after the truce ends; Ukraine blames Russia for fake nuclear warnings.
Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of Trump pressure, the Guardian reports; the Kremlin says Kyiv is ignoring US wishes.
Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Ukraine during a localized US-brokered ceasefire.
US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, with $2.1 billion to be paid by allies.
Russia fires three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv; Downing Street and Zelenskyy rebuke Witkoff for calling Putin a 'humanitarian'.
CNBC: Musk's clash with Ukraine accelerates demand for Starlink alternatives, but few exist.
Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees in principle to resume peace talks; Trump says the world is 'the closest we've been' to ending the war.
Trump links his Russia sanctions waiver to the release of jailed American Stephen Hubbard.
Russia to send its first diesel tanker to the US on Thursday under the Trump deal.
Putin tells Witkoff he agrees in principle to resume trilateral talks; Russia releases American Stephen Hubbard.
Witkoff to present Putin an updated proposal in St. Petersburg Wednesday, a US official says; Kushner to join virtually.

storylines.title: AI debt worries and market selloff
storylines.summary: After Democrats won Congress, AI stocks plunged: the Nasdaq had its worst day since April 2025 as chip and neocloud shares fell on fears of a slower data center buildout. SpaceX credit risk hit a record; AI firms are offering concessions.

events.text: CNBC: chip stocks and neoclouds plunge, pushing the Nasdaq to its worst day since April 2025 on fears of a post-midterm AI slowdown.
Asian tech stocks slide on fears Democratic control slows data center buildout; Hong Kong rebounds as investors rotate away from AI hardware.
The Hill reports data centers lost overwhelmingly where they were on the ballot; Ars Technica says Big Tech calls the backlash anti-Trump, not anti-tech.
Voters approve dozens of data center moratoriums; hyperscalers and Apple surge while chipmakers and data center stocks fall, CNBC and the FT report.
Stocks and the dollar fall as Democrats win Congress; traders fear tighter AI oversight and slower data center buildout, the FT reports.
Meta seeks to raise $20 billion to $25 billion in a bond sale for AI spending.
AMD jumps 8% as data center revenue nearly doubles; Palantir and Shopify fall after earnings.
Nasdaq-100 tumbles into its third correction this year as AI worries mount, MarketWatch reports; Blackstone's Jon Gray calls for more equity to fund AI.
FT says the global AI selloff eases after the Nasdaq's worst month in over a year; US stock futures gain in Asian trading.
FT reports a junk debt rout sparking a 'bloodbath' for credit investors; Bloomberg says investors brace for more volatile days after the tech rout.
Bloomberg: AI enthusiasm is collapsing and Big Tech earnings made it worse; CNBC says stocks reversed from early-week gains.
OpenAI pares fundraising goal to as much as $20 billion; S&P turns negative on Meta; Intel has worst day since the 1970s.
Meta falls 6% as AI spending pushes free cash flow negative and its credit default swaps hit records; tech stocks slide.
Treasury yields sink below 5% as investors seek safety from AI fallout, MarketWatch reports.
DeepSeek reportedly raises $15 billion days after US federal restrictions.
Stocks fall as megacap earnings fail to reassure on AI; Treasuries and yen rally as havens and Chinese equities near a bear market.
Meta says it will issue a new class of non-voting shares, trading from 2027, to fund AI initiatives, acquisitions and pay.
SpaceX shares jump about 10% on earnings and Tesla merger talk, while its bonds weaken on debt fears.
Nebius says AI computing prices are rising as investors question neocloud debt and economics.
Stocks rise as strong tech earnings revive the AI trade after last week's selloff; oil gains.

storylines.title: Fed under Warsh weighs further hikes
storylines.summary: After a September hike, the Fed under Chairman Kevin Warsh held in October. Kalshi traders put a December 25bp hike at 81%. ADP shows 86,000 private jobs added in October; with Democrats controlling the Senate, Trump's push to reshape the Fed board looks stalled.

events.text: ADP says private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, slightly above expectations.
Axios reports Trump's effort to replace Fed governors with allies looks dead now that Democrats control the Senate.
September job openings rise to 7.52 million, above the 7.15 million consensus, ahead of the payrolls report.
NPR: GDP growth is up but so are prices; interest rates are staying the same for now, with midterms ahead.
Axios: traders bet oil prices stay elevated longer, threatening to prolong inflation pressure.
CNBC reports housing data worsened in September as the Fed weighs more rate hikes; Axios says homebuilder sentiment is at a 14-year low.
MarketWatch says the October decision is a closer call than markets think, weighing arguments against a hike.
Warsh says the economy has performed largely as expected since the September hike; markets expect a hold.

storylines.title: 2026 midterm elections
storylines.summary: Democrats won the House, Senate and most governorships. Mississippi (Colom leads by about 1,000) and Alaska (Sullivan-Peltola, with a namesake candidate dispute) remain uncalled. Jeffries seeks speaker; Johnson steps aside; Schumer faces leadership pressure. Trump and Vance blame the Iran war.

events.text: Trump says Sen. Dan Sullivan should receive the votes cast for namesake Dan J. Sullivan in Alaska, where the margin is 642 votes.
BBC: Democrat Scott Colom leads Cindy Hyde-Smith by just over 1,000 votes in Mississippi; Republicans pin hopes on late-arriving ballots.
Scott Wiener is poised to win Pelosi's seat; Nithya Raman is projected to unseat Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, per Decision Desk HQ.
Sen. Ted Cruz says Republicans did not grasp cost-of-living concerns and calls Democratic Texas wins a 'blue tsunami'.
Peltola leads Sullivan by 626 first-choice votes in Alaska; Colom leads Hyde-Smith by 1,138 in Mississippi. Both races remain uncalled.
Hakeem Jeffries formally announces his bid for House speaker, saying Democrats expect at least 255 seats.
Vance says the Iran war cost Republicans the midterms; Trump later calls it the primary reason but says he would do it again.
Speaker Mike Johnson will not stay on as House Republican leader; Scalise and Jordan eye the job.
Democrats outline investigations of the Trump administration while promising an affordability focus.
Mississippi Senate race between Scott Colom and Cindy Hyde-Smith remains too close to call.
Democrats flip Senate seats in Kansas, Iowa, South Carolina, North Carolina and Maine, and win the House's 218th seat, taking both chambers.
Democrat James Talarico defeats Ken Paxton to win the Texas Senate seat, the first Democratic Senate win there since 1988.
Trump says he is willing to accept the results but Republicans would have won in a landslide if he were on the ballot.
Trump-backed Ed Gallrein is projected to win Rep. Thomas Massie's Kentucky seat, per Decision Desk HQ.
First polls close; Westchester County machines reject paper ballots, which will still be counted.
DOJ reportedly sends target letters to about 20 Democrats, including Marc Elias, over the alleged decoy Dan Sullivan candidacy.
Rep. Haley Stevens requests US marshals' protection after death threats over her Rogers endorsement, Axios reports.
Supreme Court rejects the Trump administration's emergency bid to set aside about 20,000 California ballots, with no noted dissents.
Axios says final polls, models and markets forecast Democratic gains; Cook shifts Michigan Senate to lean Democratic.
Stevens is removed from the Michigan Democratic Party, Washington Examiner reports; some House Democrats seek her removal from caucus, Axios reports.

storylines.title: US-Iran war and oil prices
storylines.summary: Iran says five tankers and a tugboat caught fire in Hormuz amid fears of a new US attack. Oil fell below $100 earlier this week on hopes a Democratic Congress will push to end the war; 23 US service members have died.

events.text: Iran says five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in several incidents in the Strait of Hormuz amid fears of a new US attack.
Axios says Trump, who blames the war for GOP losses, faces mostly bad options: strike again or seek a deal.
South Korea plans to extend its anti-piracy unit's area closer to the Strait of Hormuz after Trump criticism over Iran war support.
Oil steadies after falling more than 8% as investors bet a Democratic sweep could accelerate efforts to end the war.
Defense News reports two US airmen died in non-hostile incidents last week, raising the war's US death toll to 23.
Oil falls below $100 as Vance blames the Iran war for GOP losses and traders see pressure for an offramp.
Schumer says Democrats will use the power of the purse to end the Iran war; Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted no to war.
Iran calls the US reply to its Hormuz plan unconvincing as indirect talks continue; Trump confirms a strike on an Iranian anti-aircraft facility.
Trump tells the FT the US has no immediate plan to strike Iran and calls his position brilliant; oil edges higher.
Yemen's government accuses Iran's IRGC and Hezbollah of sending 21 experts to back the Houthis.
US strikes radar and missile launchers on Iran's Qeshm Island, officials say defensively, a day before the midterms; oil steady.
Trump tells Axios he is 'in no rush' to decide whether to resume fighting in Iran.
Oil declines after a report Trump wants to give Iran diplomacy more time before possibly resuming strikes after the midterms, Bloomberg says.
FT: Gulf states brace for escalation between the US-Israel alliance and Iran; diplomats warn renewed conflict would be more damaging than earlier rounds.
Gulf leaders meet in Qatar as mediators await Washington's reply to an Iranian proposal involving $6 billion in assets and reopening Hormuz.
Axios: Trump has a frank call with Netanyahu about how quickly to return to combat; Netanyahu presses for strikes.
Trump says the US is not in much of a hurry for an Iran deal; Araghchi says Iran and Qatar have a plan to reopen Hormuz in two days.
Qatari mediators hold 12-plus hours of talks in Tehran to restart US-Iran negotiations; talks continue in Doha.
Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei orders an immediate response without geographical limits to any US or Israeli attack.
Oil jumps to a five-month high as Iran's IRGC says it hit four vessels in the northern Gulf and three ships struck mines near Hormuz.

storylines.title: Binance $6.3 billion hack
storylines.summary: Binance says suspected North Korean hackers used fake job interviews and a tampered installer to steal $6.3 billion after months of planning, and that 98% of affected assets are replenished. North Korea denies involvement.

events.text: Binance says the hackers spent months planning, using laptop infections, compromised internal tooling and fake job interviews.
North Korea fires multiple missiles and Kim Yo Jong rejects dialogue with the US while denying responsibility for the hack.
Binance's postmortem says hackers used fake job interviews and an internal AI tool; it says 98% of affected assets are replenished.
North Korea denies being behind the hack; the FT reports hackers are expected to take months to launder the funds.
Binance users withdraw $3.6 billion after the exchange resumes transactions following the largest-ever crypto hack, the BBC reports.
Binance resumes phased withdrawals; TechCrunch reports 95% of stolen assets covered, while Binance's own figure reported elsewhere is 90%.
Binance says 90% of losses are covered and withdrawals resume Sunday; FBI says North Korea-backed TraderTraitor is behind the attack.

storylines.title: Israel election deadlock
storylines.summary: Israel's election produced a deadlock, with Arab parties holding the balance. Netanyahu claims the vote was 'stolen'; the election body says results stand. Arab parties now back Gadi Eisenkot, and Herzog decides within a week whom to task.

events.text: Arab parties led by Yousef Jabareen tell Herzog they back Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form a government.
Herzog accepts the vote results and opens talks on forming a government, a blow to Netanyahu's efforts to discredit the election, Al Jazeera reports.
President Herzog begins consultations with parties and warns not every promise can be fulfilled if they want to avoid another election.
Israel's election body says the deadlocked result will stand even if foreign-interference claims are proven, as Netanyahu alleges the election was 'stolen'.
Arab coalition leader Yousef Jabareen says he is ready to join the opposition bloc to oust Netanyahu after record seat gains, the Guardian reports.
